messages:
sam_sales: Heads up - Client (Northway) on Dedicated trial reports missing trace_id in S3 export and backend shows some 429 spikes. Can we triage?
client_it: confirmed. We ingest to /v1/export and then run a Splunk forwarder from S3. Many of the ndjson lines lack "trace_id" so Splunk can't join logs<>traces. Also saw HTTP 429s in our client logs during a 14:10 load test.
leo_solutions: tagging taylor & anika. Quick Q: are they using the SDK that sets X-Request-Id vs a custom trace header?
taylor_sre: likely propagation gap. Two usual culprits: 1) exporter concurrency causing race and dropping the trace field when fanout writes happen in parallel, 2) upstream not sending a consistent trace header.
anika_se: Northway is on a per-tenant route (route id: northway-prod). Can you paste a sample event from S3?
client_it: sample ndjson (redacted):
```json
{"ts":"2024-10-12T14:10:05Z","service":"frontend","msg":"user search","attrs":{"status":200,"path":"/search"}}
```
sam_sales: And their simple test curl looks like:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/export \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'X-Request-Id: 7a8b9c0d-1234' \
  -d '{"event":"foo"}'
```
taylor_sre: ask them to set X-Redwood-Trace or X-Cloud-Trace-Context with their trace id. We have a mapping for either header. Also enable preserve_trace_context on their route to keep header->trace mapping through parallel exporter writes.
leo_solutions: how to flip preserve_trace_context?
taylor_sre: admin API (example):
```http
PATCH /v1/routes/northway-prod
{"preserve_trace_context": true, "exporters": ["splunk","s3"]}
```
beth_security: also flagging the KMS bits - Dedicated requires a CMK ARN for customer-managed SSE on S3 exports. I'll DM the exact policy they need to attach to the Redwood service principal.
anika_se: FYI Northway used the default export_batch_size (10). For high fanout to Splunk + S3 we recommend increasing export_batch_size to 30 and set export_concurrency to 2 to avoid write storms.
client_it: can that be toggled without downtime? We are mid-trial.
taylor_sre: yes it's a live config change. I'll patch the route and scale sampling to 100% briefly so they can validate trace join, then scale down to 20% after 20m.
deploy-bot: route patch requested: routes/northway-prod -> {preserve_trace_context:true, export_batch_size:30, export_concurrency:2} (deploy id d-9127)
deploy-bot: deploy d-9127: started
deploy-bot: deploy d-9127: succeeded :white_check_mark:
client_it: retested right after deploy 1: Splunk now shows trace_id on ~99% of joined events, S3 ndjson includes "trace_id" field. The 429s dropped during the test.
beth_security: sending CMK onboarding checklist + required IAM policy to client security. Note: for Dedicated we can accept an S3 bucket policy with PutObject condition bound to the CMK.
leo_solutions: I'll schedule a security handoff call with Northway for Thursday 9am PT. Also capturing follow-ups: a) confirm CMK ARN b) confirm Splunk forwarder configuration reads ndjson trace_id field c) we keep route at 100% sampling for 15m then 20% for steady-state.
taylor_sre: adding temporary alert: exporter-429-count > 5 in 1m -> page SRE. Also added dashboard panel: Console > Observability > Exporters > northway-prod > Last 1h traces with trace_id missing.
sam_sales: great. Northway legal also requested a short note on what data leaves Redwood in exports (we exported list + example payload). Anika, can you draft a one-pager we can attach?
anika_se: will do, sending draft in this thread in 30m.
client_it: thanks team. Looks much better. We'll confirm CMK ARN later today.
sam_sales: closing the swarm once we verify CMK and sampling ramp. Thanks all!
